title: Pavel Durov at Oslo Freedom Forum: how governments erode freedom, and why privacy has to be defended
summary: A political keynote, not a growth talk. Durov draws on 20 years of running VK and Telegram to argue that governments use child-protection pretexts, mass surveillance and selective enforcement to control platforms. The product and leadership lessons are indirect: refuse political deals, don't hold user data you can't protect, and expect bans to fail.

principles.text: Bans on a popular platform fail: users route around them with VPNs, so a product people value survives blocking.
principles.quote: 95% of Russian teenagers still use Telegram every month. How? They use VPNs. They bypass the entire thing.

principles.text: Treat 'protect the children' as a common pretext for control; judge laws by their stated aims, not their justification.
principles.quote: They used protection of children as a pretext, where in fact in fact, they wanted more control over political speech online.

principles.text: Don't trade essential liberty for temporary safety. Weakening privacy rarely stops crime, because criminals switch tools first.
principles.quote: The criminals will be the first to switch on to other tools, more secure. It will be the law-abiding citizens who will be put in danger.

principles.text: Collecting more user data than you can protect creates danger. Data held will leak or be abused.
principles.quote: The government wanted too much data and failed to protect it. And now they want more of the data.

principles.text: A founder must resist selective enforcement: stay loyal to users' rights even when refusing political demands invites persecution.
principles.quote: If the business owner decides to stand up for the constitutional rights of his or her fellow citizens, if they refuse to cave in to political demands... then the persecution and the enforcement of laws comes in full.

principles.text: In an AI era, giving up privacy means total scalable surveillance, so private messaging must be defended now.
principles.quote: In the world of AI, if we give up our right to privacy, you can be certain that every message that you send will be monitored, will be analyzed.
